correctness.rationale: The exact integral polynomial identity follows from congruence semi-invariance, determinant of the Sym^2 representation, and a block Hessian at identity. The gradient equals diagonal adjugate cofactors and twice off-diagonal adjugate cofactors; rank-one adjugates rule out corank-one base points, and inverse alternating forms characterize the extra even characteristic-two full-rank base component. Nonsingular symmetric bilinear-form classification and the explicit quadratic terms at corank one/two give all Hessian ranks, with corank at least three having vanishing 2-jet. The embedded check_hessian.py verifies finite instances n=3,4 but is not used as an infinite proof. Boundaries n>=3; upper triangular independent variables; fields algebraically closed for orbit type, characteristic any.

value.rationale: The generic symmetric determinant is a canonical determinantal hypersurface and polar Cremona map. The theorem locates a geometrically meaningful positive-characteristic boundary: an entire component of indeterminacy formed by invertible alternating matrices can exist outside the determinant hypersurface in even size, and identically vanishing ordinary Hessian can coexist with birational gradient in odd characteristic. Exact universal Hessian rank by matrix corank and bilinear form type is useful for understanding degeneracy strata, modular polar-map pathology, and characteristic-sensitive singular geometry; it is not an arbitrary finite invariant or routine fixed-case recomputation.
